meta.title: Questions, unknowns and suggestions, for review before anything is implemented
meta.how_to_use: Read the questions first. A question is listed because a decision cannot be made without it. Each suggestion names the question it waits on, so nothing on this page has to be implemented to be evaluated.

questions.question: Is there any source that publishes official NFL prices (opening or closing)?
questions.what_we_know: No. The scores and schedules pages publish results and links, not prices; the source check is confirmed. Every price in this repository is third-party.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether a licensed price vendor could be contracted, and at what cost.
questions.how_to_close: Either contract a licensed feed and record its licence, or accept third-party prices and mark every CLV figure as third-party on the site forever.
questions.owner_action: a sourcing decision only you can make

questions.question: Which books, jurisdictions and limits are actually available to you?
questions.what_we_know: None have been verified. The executable gate has never been satisfied, which is why nothing is live.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Country, licence, stake limits, and whether same-game parlays are even offered in your jurisdiction.
questions.how_to_close: Name one book and one jurisdiction; the executable gate can then be tested once instead of assumed.

questions.question: Can an opening number be recorded for the moneyline at all?
questions.what_we_know: The upstream opening-line file has zero MONEYLINE rows. It carries one sportsbook and one season (2021).
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether any accessible source records an opening moneyline with a timestamp and a book.
questions.how_to_close: Locate a source with opening moneylines before promising CLV on the moneyline.

questions.question: Does an official source publish depth-chart order (1st/2nd/3rd string)?
questions.what_we_know: Not on the team roster page and not on the injury report; both were read and neither has a depth column.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether the league publishes it anywhere accessible, or whether a team-by-team scrape is the only route.
questions.how_to_close: Check the league's roster/depth publication directly, or accept third-party depth and label it.

questions.question: Does the market still move after the snapshot we record?
questions.what_we_know: The extract's prices are described as closing, but the timestamp is not published with the row; the hold is about 4.2% on the current board.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: The exact minute each price was true.
questions.how_to_close: Record a timestamp with every price, even a third-party one.

questions.question: Can prop prices be obtained, so prop ROI is measurable at all?
questions.what_we_know: The repository holds no historical prop prices, so no prop ROI has ever been computed. Prop combos are priced with model probabilities, not market prices.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether any vendor sells historical prop prices back far enough to test.
questions.how_to_close: Price the data before pricing the strategy.

questions.question: What is the minimum sample a strategy must reach before it can be called live?
questions.what_we_know: The static gates require n>=1000 settled bets, and the project's own power analysis needs about 10,598 bets to detect a 3% edge.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether a smaller sample with a larger edge would be acceptable, and who decides.
questions.how_to_close: Choose between the strict gate and a staged paper->live path with a smaller sample and a tighter demotion.

questions.question: Should the leaderboard rank on signal, staking, or both?
questions.what_we_know: 2 of 9 strategies show a positive ROI their own significance test does not support.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether you want the leaderboard to motivate (staking) or to inform (signal).
questions.how_to_close: Pick the ranking column; the data now supports either.

questions.question: What happens to a live strategy that stops working?
questions.what_we_know: Until this build, nothing did. Eight demotion rules now exist with explicit triggers and actions.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether the demotion thresholds are tight enough; four of the eight rules are not evaluable today.
questions.how_to_close: Run the rules on paper for a season and count how often each fires.

questions.question: Are injuries and depth priced in by the model at all?
questions.what_we_know: No. The originated lines take no injury or depth input; the depth page is descriptive and separate.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: How much of the model's 0.68-point spread MAE gap to the market is exactly this missing input.
questions.how_to_close: Add a depth feature behind a walk-forward test and measure the MAE change.

questions.question: Is a 2026 part-season enough to measure skill persistence?
questions.what_we_know: Year-over-year point-differential persistence from the official tables is 0.5031, but the 2026 side is 8-9 games.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether that ordering survives a full season.
questions.how_to_close: Recompute after Week 18; the code already does it from two official pages.

questions.question: Is a reward pool funded, and who judges it?
questions.what_we_know: No pool is funded and no strategy has qualified. Every published reward is 0.
questions.what_we_do_not_know: Whether rewards are symbolic, funded, or dropped entirely.
questions.how_to_close: Decide whether the competition has a prize before designing around one.

suggestions.title: Timestamp every price and reject any bet settled on an untimestamped price
suggestions.problem: A price without a time is not a price you could have taken.
suggestions.change: Add price_time and book columns to the snapshot store; every settlement joins on them and the backtest refuses rows without them.
suggestions.measure_of_success: 100% of settled bets carry a price_time and a book.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Q1 is answered, or the store will only ever hold third-party times.

suggestions.title: Buy or drop prop prices; stop pricing prop combos with model probabilities
suggestions.problem: A model probability is not a price. Prop combos currently cannot yield an ROI at all.
suggestions.change: Either source historical prop prices or remove the prop ROI column and label the page as unpriceable.
suggestions.measure_of_success: Every prop combo row has a market price or explicitly none.

suggestions.title: Stage promotion: paper, then live, with a hard bet cap while in paper
suggestions.problem: Ten gates on 1,000+ bets is a high bar that will approve almost nothing; a lower bar with no staging approves too much.
suggestions.change: Add a three-state path (paper, capped live, full live) where demotion is automatic.
suggestions.measure_of_success: A strategy can fail its way back to paper without human action.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Q4 and Q9 are answered, because the cap depends on real limits.

suggestions.title: Publish CLV against the closing line only where a real closing number exists
suggestions.problem: CLV is the strongest skill measure available, and it needs two numbers from the same book.
suggestions.change: Compute CLV per bet against the closing snapshot; leave it blank where the closing row is absent instead of substituting a different book.
suggestions.measure_of_success: CLV published with n, and blanks where the closing number is missing.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Q1 is answered about the book identity.

suggestions.title: Two-column leaderboard: signal rank and staking rank, never one blended score
suggestions.problem: A blended score hides exactly the case the user asked about: a lucky staking run masking a bad signal.
suggestions.change: Show signal rank (significance) and staking rank (return) side by side, and reward only when both clear their own bar.
suggestions.measure_of_success: No strategy can rank above another on staking alone.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Q5 is answered (it is a preference, not a fact).

suggestions.title: Make depth a model input behind a walk-forward test, not a separate page
suggestions.problem: The depth work is descriptive today; it changes no number the model produces.
suggestions.change: Feed a weighted depth-lost term into the ridge engine on a walk-forward basis and report the MAE change out of sample.
suggestions.measure_of_success: Out-of-sample spread MAE falls versus the current 10.39 points.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Q3 is answered, so the feature has a source you trust.

suggestions.title: Pre-register every new correlation before computing it
suggestions.problem: Trying many pairs and publishing the big ones is how a false signal gets built.
suggestions.change: Write the pair, the units, the n and the threshold to a file first; the build fails if an unregistered pair appears in the output.
suggestions.measure_of_success: 0 correlations published without a prior registration row.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Nothing; this is safe to do now.

suggestions.title: Make the executable gate a hard, named, one-time test
suggestions.problem: Every strategy fails gate G9 because no book, licence or limit was ever verified. That is an unanswered question, not a strategy defect.
suggestions.change: Record one verified book, jurisdiction and limit, then re-test G9 as a yes/no.
suggestions.measure_of_success: G9 evaluable for at least one strategy.
suggestions.do_not_implement_until: Q9 is answered by you; this cannot be discovered from data.

not_implemented: Nothing on this page is implemented. It is a proposal list; the numbers that support it are on the other pages and every one of them is reproducible from the committed data.
